text: Over centuries, these communities moved east into the great plain of the Ganga.
They cleared forests, farmed rice, and learned to use iron.
Villages grew into towns, towns into kingdoms.
By about 600 BCE, North India had 16 big states, the Mahajanapadas.
Thus, society was also hardening into ranked groups, priests, warriors, traders, and workers,
a system called varna which over many centuries would set into the rigid rules of caste.
And the thinkers of this age asked bigger and bigger questions.
In texts called the Upanishads, they asked, what is the self?
Is there one reality behind everything?
Of all sixteen kingdoms, one was growing faster and hungrier than the rest.
And two young princes of this age were about to walk away from their palaces
and change the world without fighting a single war.
